Karadzic says: Could there be a buffer zone between them? Kukanjac says: Let's see. We are in contact with them with this Koprivica person to see what's going on. Karadzic said: So please send someone. They're afraid of the military. Let there be a buffer zone between them. The military is welcome here in that sense. Does this tally with what you know about our expectations on the army part?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR STANIC
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Okay. I've made this objection repeatedly. This is clearly a pattern. So Dr. Karadzic shows the witness a document he clearly hasn't seen before and it takes clearly the form of a leading question. He needs to lay a foundation. It's difficult to understand in any event how a document like this is going to be successfully used in the course of redirect but certainly not in this manner to lead the witness through this document and just simply ask him to affirm aspects of it that tally with what the accused wants him to say.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have an answer?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I'm convinced that this arises from cross-examination about the nature of the attack and our intents with the industrial facilities in Vogosca. In terms of the basis, I put a question --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger is not challenging that -- the fact that you are entitled to ask and put -- pose questions with respect to the attack on Pretis. He was challenging the way you're posing the questions.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It seemed to me that Mr. Tieger disputed the foundation. I can't find it, in which line, but in any case, I will refrain from --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Without leading -- putting some foundational questions or -- if you put this document to the witness and ask a question whether it's consistent with his understanding, that's a typically -- a leading question.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have determined the foundation, because there was the issue of attack on Pretis and our intentions with Pretis, because that was touched upon in cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: My question is: What do you have to say about this conversation of mine with General Kukanjac?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR STANIC
utterances.text: It is my opinion that you acted correctly.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Excuse me. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: He answered that question a while ago. Shall we move on, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You were asked about the bunker. You were also asked about the Sonjas. And you said you didn't know about the bunker. What is this Sonja's place? Can you repeat that for us?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR STANIC
utterances.text: It used to be called the Kon Tiki motel, which had five rooms and a restaurant. It's a motel. It was called Sonja's or Kon Tiki. It was owned by Sonja. The Crisis Staff was in communication with her son Zeljko Beganovic at some point in time asking that the facility be made available for us. I don't know whether he was present there at the time.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we have P2398. Could we please zoom in and have the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this the motel, and why did the Crisis Staff want to have the motel at its disposal, to house which institution?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR STANIC
utterances.text: It's an order. We see that the motel was called Kon Tiki, and it was owned by Sonja. It was provided to the public security station of Vogosca municipality and to the TO. So it was requested that premises be made available in order to bring in and question certain persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you distinguish between prison and detention unit?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR STANIC
utterances.text: Yes, as I have said, we never had the appropriate conditions for prison but a detention unit is temporary and from that unit we would send people on to Kula for further processing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Who carried out those investigations in Kon Tiki?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR STANIC
utterances.text: Lawyers as a whole with Zdravko Luketa and I think the prison warden. I don't really know who the interviewer or interrogator was, Mr. Vlaco Spiro. I don't know. I can't remember, but it was a judicial authority who was involved in the interrogations.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What was the comfort like in Kon Tiki?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR STANIC
utterances.text: It was good. There were four or five rooms there, double beds. There was a restaurant on the ground floor 11 [as interpreted] with all the facilities and there were rooms on the floors.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Does this order state that some sort of a bunker is to be commandeered?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR STANIC
utterances.text: No. This order has nothing to do with the bunker.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you tell the Chamber whose name is printed there? Well, you can see it. Could you tell them who signed it?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR STANIC
utterances.text: On behalf of the president it was signed by Slavko Jovanovic, and Jovan Tintor was the president of the Crisis Staff and this was of the Crisis Staff. This was the decision taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. As for the municipal authorities in conditions of war when there is an imminent threat of war, do they have the right to commandeer certain facilities, features for the authorities?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR STANIC
utterances.text: Yes. This is regulated by the law. They can temporarily commandeer certain facilities to be used for certain purposes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Although you were not involved in this as you have said, as far as you knew after interrogations and investigations had been carried out, what were the possible outcomes? What might happen to the detainees?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR STANIC
utterances.text: After the interrogations had been completed, well, I wasn't involved in that process, but it was always said that if there was no proof that someone had been involved in some kind of a crime or misdemeanour that person would be released. If there were any indications that a crime had been committed then these people would be transferred to the Kula two or three days later when it was possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could we see P2367, please. Could you please have a look at this list of detained Muslims and tell us whether there is women among these names?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR STANIC
utterances.text: I can't see. Let me just have a look. Just a moment. No, there -- there is no woman there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you count how many of them were there?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR STANIC
utterances.text: One two, three, nine, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And to the right?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR STANIC
utterances.text: To the right, to the right, the names to the left, I can't see them, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Have a look at the English version.

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR STANIC
utterances.text: The English version I can't see anything to the left.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is there a Besirevic on the right-hand side?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR STANIC
utterances.text: Besirevic, no. Yes, yes, there is a Besirevic. I do apologise. Eleven, 12, 15. There are 15.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And they were released for how many Serbs?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR STANIC
utterances.text: Two or three -- three Serbs. In exchange for three Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was this an exception or was it quite usual for us to give more for less?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR STANIC
utterances.text: Well, we always released more of them. Whenever they would register for an exchange, Luketa made certain proposals to that effect. I think that he said if anyone wants to leave and go to Vogosca they should go. They gave three in exchange. Whether this was an exception or not, I don't know. I believe it was an exception. I can't remember the -- but the decision was that the exchanges should be on the one-for-one basis, but this -- in this case this number of persons was exchanged for three persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I just have another question. At the republican town and municipal level was there commission for exchanges?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR STANIC
utterances.text: Yes, there was a commission for exchanges on all these levels on the town level, on the republican level, on the municipal level.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stanic for your testimony.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellencies, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That concludes your evidence, Mr. Stanic. On behalf of the Chamber I thank you for coming to The Hague to give it. Now you're free to go.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. If you would allow me to shake the President's hand, it would be an honour for me. If not, well ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No. Thank you, Mr. Stanic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Excellencies, I would like to address you for a few minutes and then I see time probably we should start with the next witness next morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I'd like to apologise for my reaction. However, I have to say that it's -- this legal system is a significant problem for all of us. This system in which various skills are allowed for the Prosecution, that wouldn't be permissible in our system. And one of the significant problems that this Tribunal is facing will be the fact that we are subjected to a judicial system that doesn't resemble anything that is familiar to us. And therefore these skills of trying to outfox someone while the accused is sitting here, well, for us it's strange. I know it's allowed here, but in our system it's not permissible to twist a question and obtain a positive answer to such a question, because no witness is sufficiently concentrated to be able to -- to see when the Prosecution is acting in a cunning manner.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't agree with your observation at all, Mr. Karadzic. If I can simply react to that. If you're not capable of coping with the Defence, Mr. Harvey is there to take up the case if necessary. Judge Morrison has a point for you, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Well, at the risk of taking more time than I intended, I have several points. It's not that difficult in reality, Dr. Karadzic. The first and most basic point is that re-examination must relate to an issue raised in cross-examination. Either it does or it does not, and you are well capable of determining that. Secondly, you must ask non-leading foundation questions before you put a document to a witness that hasn't previously been before him or her. If the witness has no knowledge of that document or the matters contained within it, there is almost certainly no proper basis for adducing that document in re-examination or indeed at all. If, as has happened several times, you ask a question and do not like the answer, that is, I fear, the dilemma of an advocate in any system. What you cannot do is to put a leading question or comment to try and get the witness to agree with the material being subsequently fed to him or her. Not only is that improper, the Court is very unlikely to give any favourable response to material that comes before it in that way; it is, therefore, a waste of time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Judge Baird also has a point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Dr. Karadzic, I just want to add just a small bit to what Judge Morrison has said. I don't think it's fair to Mr. Tieger to say that he's acting in a cunning manner - I don't think so at all - and he was trying to outfox someone whilst you were sitting there. I think I apprehend what Mr. Tieger was insisting on is that you ask questions that are governed by the rules of re-examination. I think that was the main thrust of his -- of his objection. I don't think he was acting in a cunning manner at all.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I absolutely do agree, and I do accept that, but my apology has to do with my reaction in the course of the cross-examination. Why was I upset? I called this military cunning, but it wasn't derogatory. In this system it's permissible to try and outfox someone. That's not permissible in our system. The judge would immediately warn someone if that person was trying to confuse the witness. But what has been said about redirect, well, I absolutely accept all of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And in the future, please bear in mind what I have said during the hearing, that before you make your submission, please let us know that you have an objection. Yes, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. President, but just one last thing. Dr. Karadzic is referring, I believe, to a particular question during cross-examination. It is inconceivable that there is a distinction between the adversarial system and the continental system in trying to get at the truth, and when an examiner asks a witness whether or not the language that appears in a particular document in fact is a reference to something that's not explicitly mentioned, that's entirely fair. The suggestion that Dr. Karadzic repeatedly makes that there is some fundamental distinction between those two systems which handicaps him here is, I think, patently untrue. Both system try in their own way to get at the truth. That's all that I was trying to do here, as I believe the Court could see, and I must say this is the first time I've ever been the object of an apology that insisted I was being cunning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: The point is well taken, Mr. Tieger. Perhaps you would prefer to be known as the silver fox.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I will take that in mind and hope that's the last time I hear it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just for planning purposes, is it still the case Mr. Vujasin's testimony is fixed on Thursday?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: It is, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So it's not possible to hear -- to start him tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Given the time, we will adjourn for today and resume tomorrow morning at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 19th day of December, 2012, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.40 p.m.,
